answer: The sable multiplier is published, charged in nadir, and nectar lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 583 identities would post 4017 proofs and burn roughly 70 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
